title: Session
description: One chat conversation. Postgres creates it ('session:<thread_id>') when the first user message of a ui/telegram/api thread is checkpointed; the runtime writes 'content' (the IRC-style transcript) and 'last_activity' after each turn. Progenitor reads and edits it as a file under /sessions/; only the type's writable fields can be changed.

source.description: Where the conversation started: the app, Telegram, or a direct Responses API caller.

title.description: The stored title. "New chat" until someone renames it; the sidebar then shows the first message instead.

first_message.description: Text of the user's opening message without the machine-only attachment note, capped at 4000 characters. "* sends an attachment" when it was only attachments, "* sends an image" when it was only images.

created_at.description: When the first message was checkpointed.

last_activity.description: When the latest turn finished (created_at until then).

content.description: IRC-style transcript, rendered by the runtime after each turn. Empty until the first turn finishes.
